cards.concept: Functional dependency: what does X → Y mean?
cards.intuition: Treat X as a reliable lookup label for Y. Whenever two rows share X, they must share Y; if X is not a key, copying Y beside every repeated X creates redundancy.
cards.formula: X → Y means equal X values imply equal Y values

cards.intuition: First make values individually addressable, then ensure each fact needs the entire key, then ensure it depends on no other non-key fact. It is a sequence for finding facts stored beside the wrong entity.
cards.formula: 1NF: atomic values; 2NF: no partial-key dependency; 3NF: no transitive non-key dependency

cards.concept: Why does sale-time unit_price belong on an order line?
cards.intuition: A product list price can change, but the price actually paid describes one historical sale. Putting it only on the product would rewrite history whenever the current price changed.
cards.formula: store a fact with the entity and time it truly describes

cards.concept: The three anomalies caused by redundant facts
cards.intuition: Copies can disagree during an update, a fact may be impossible to insert without an unrelated host row, and deleting the host can erase an unrelated fact. Normalization gives each fact an independent home.
cards.formula: update anomaly + insertion anomaly + deletion anomaly

cards.concept: Why does normalization make inconsistency structurally harder?
cards.intuition: When one fact has one authoritative row, writers cannot update only some of its copies because there are no copies. Atomic single-row changes replace coordination across many redundant cells.

cards.concept: When is redundant data safe enough to serve?
cards.intuition: A read-only copy that is deterministically rebuilt from a normalized source behaves like a cache. It may lag, but it cannot become an independently hand-edited rival truth.
cards.formula: safe derived copy = authoritative source + automated idempotent rebuild

cards.intuition: Instead of rejoining tables on every read, join once during loading and store the wide result. It is like preassembling a frequently ordered kit: storage and refresh work buy cheaper repeated reads.
cards.formula: denormalization moves join work from read time to write time
cards.topic: Deliberate Denormalization: Paying Storage to Eliminate Joins

cards.concept: Why is denormalization especially attractive in warehouses?
cards.intuition: One batch load can support thousands of reads, while columnar encoding makes repeated low-cardinality attributes compact. Avoiding repeated distributed shuffles usually saves more than the extra bytes cost.
cards.formula: prefer when reads greatly outnumber writes and refresh is controlled
cards.topic: Deliberate Denormalization: Paying Storage to Eliminate Joins

cards.concept: System of record versus denormalized serving model
cards.intuition: The normalized source is the ledger; the wide table or chunk corpus is a fast photocopy. Repair the photocopy by rebuilding it from the ledger, never by making it a second ledger.
cards.formula: normalized source = truth; denormalized model = derived artifact
cards.topic: Deliberate Denormalization: Paying Storage to Eliminate Joins

cards.concept: How do STRUCT and ARRAY denormalize one-to-many data?
cards.intuition: Children live inside their parent as typed repeated records. Parent fields are stored once, yet the engine still understands every nested leaf as a queryable typed column.
cards.formula: ARRAY<STRUCT<...>> = typed repeated child records inside one parent row
cards.topic: Nested and Repeated Fields (STRUCT/ARRAY) as Modern Denormalization

cards.concept: What does UNNEST do to grain?
cards.intuition: UNNEST opens a parent's child array and emits one row per element, carrying the parent context with each. It recreates child grain only for queries that need it.
cards.formula: UNNEST(array) expands one parent row into one row per array element
cards.topic: Nested and Repeated Fields (STRUCT/ARRAY) as Modern Denormalization

cards.concept: When should children remain a separate table?
cards.intuition: Separate them when they are queried alone, updated independently, or shared across parents. Nest them when they arrive with the parent and are overwhelmingly read through it.
cards.formula: nest parent-bound children; separate first-class independent entities
cards.topic: Nested and Repeated Fields (STRUCT/ARRAY) as Modern Denormalization
